verifyNotes: Confirm against the official exam page (databricks.com/learn/certification/machine-learning-associate) and the current exam guide PDF (https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/Databricks-Certified-Machine-Learning-Associate-Exam-Guide-August-2026.pdf): 48 scored items plus up to 10 unscored, 90 minutes, USD 200, online proctored or test centre, English/Japanese/pt-BR/Korean, valid 2 years, no published passing score. Weights: Databricks Machine Learning 38, Data Processing 19 (the web page calls it 'ML Workflows'), Model Development 31, Model Deployment 12. Use current names from docs.databricks.com: Databricks Runtime for ML, AutoML, Feature Engineering in Unity Catalog (online tables/online feature stores), MLflow 3, Models in Unity Catalog with aliases (champion/challenger), Mosaic AI Model Serving, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (formerly Delta Live Tables; the guide still says DLT), Spark ML. Hyperopt is in the guide but Databricks has deprecated/removed it from newer ML runtimes in favour of Optuna: check and teach both the exam wording and the current recommendation. Never copy the guide's sample questions.
name: Databricks Certified Machine Learning Associate
audience: Data scientists and ML engineers doing basic ML on Databricks, with about six months of hands-on experience
format: 48 scored multiple-choice and multiple-selection items (up to 10 more unscored) in 90 minutes; online proctored or test centre; English, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, Korean. Databricks publishes no passing score; this site uses 700 on a 100–1000 scale for its mocks.
scenarios: Real-time recommendation endpoint with A/B traffic split
Demand forecast scored nightly in batch

domains.name: Databricks Machine Learning
skills: MLOps best practices; ML runtimes; AutoML for model and feature selection; promoting code vs promoting models
Feature Engineering in Unity Catalog: creating and writing feature tables, training and scoring with features, account-level vs workspace tables, online vs offline tables
MLflow: manual logging of metrics, artifacts and models; finding the best run with the Client API; the MLflow UI; registering in Unity Catalog; tags; champion/challenger aliases

domains.name: Data Processing
skills: Summary statistics with .summary() and dbutils data summaries; outlier removal by standard deviation or IQR; visualising and comparing categorical and continuous features
Imputation with mean, median or mode; one-hot encoding and when not to use it; log transforms

domains.name: Model Development
skills: Choosing algorithms; data imbalance; estimators vs transformers; Spark ML training pipelines
Hyperparameter tuning: Hyperopt fmin (and Optuna), grid/random/Bayesian search, parallelising single-node models; cross-validation vs train-validation split and counting models trained
Classification and regression metrics (F1, log loss, ROC/AUC, RMSE, MAE, R²); choosing a metric; exponentiating log-transformed predictions; bias-variance trade-off

domains.name: Model Deployment
skills: Batch, real-time and streaming serving; pandas batch inference; streaming inference with Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (DLT)
Deploying custom models to Model Serving endpoints, querying them, and splitting traffic between models
